cards.f: Urban challenges in a developed country
cards.b: Food, energy, transport and waste demands, concentrated resource consumption and segregation.

cards.f: Urban challenges in a developing/emerging city
cards.b: Squatter settlements, informal economy, urban pollution and low quality of life.
Housing built informally on land not owned, with makeshift materials and few services such as water and sanitation.
Land never built on before, usually on the edge of a city; cheap but loses countryside.
Land previously built on, now derelict; has existing services and protects countryside but may be contaminated.
Edge of the city where housing estates, retail and business parks, and industrial estates are developed.
The separation of social, ethnic or income groups into different parts of a city.
Meets present needs without damaging the environment or the ability of future generations to meet theirs.

cards.f: Six areas for improving urban quality of life
cards.b: Waste disposal, transport, education, health, employment and housing.
Residents build or improve their own homes with materials and help from authorities, so it is cheaper.
Bus rapid transit with dedicated lanes and tube stations: cheap, fast and reduces car use.
Introduced 2003; drivers pay to enter the central zone, reducing traffic and funding public transport.
Decide land use, zoning and protect green belt; balance competing needs.
Build homes, offices and shops for profit; often prefer cheaper greenfield sites.
Scoring sites for factors such as litter, noise, traffic and greenery to compare environmental quality.

gaps.s: Land that has never been built on is a ___ site.
Derelict land that has been built on before is a ___ site.
Housing built illegally without services is a ___ settlement.
The separation of different social groups into different areas is called ___.
Curitiba is known for its bus ___ transit system.
The London ___ charge was introduced in 2003.
The edge of a city where it meets the countryside is the rural-urban ___.
A city that meets needs now without harming the future is ___.

short.q: Explain why brownfield development is preferred to greenfield development.
short.model: It reuses land with roads and services and protects countryside from urban sprawl, while regenerating run-down areas.

short.q: For a named developing or emerging city, explain two challenges.
short.model: Mumbai has squatter settlements with no sanitation causing disease, and traffic and factory pollution that cause poor air quality.

short.q: Explain how self-help schemes improve squatter settlements.
short.model: Residents get materials and services, and build safer homes themselves, which is cheaper and gives them security.

short.q: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of a congestion charge.
short.model: Advantage: reduces traffic and pollution in the centre. Disadvantage: affects low-income drivers and may push traffic to roads outside the zone.

short.q: Describe the roles of two groups in managing urban change.
short.model: Planners decide land use and protect green belt; developers build homes and shops for profit, so they may want cheaper greenfield land.
